conventions.convention: Cells are bounded Jordan-measurable sets with nodes in their cells and positive volume weights. Local finiteness, 0<h<∞, uniform local volume bounds, and the finite integration-compatible partition identity are assumptions of the rule.
An interior evaluation point satisfies B(x,Rε+2h)⊂Ω. Periodic calculations use extensions on full Euclidean space, without truncating the kernel support.

The kernel is nonnegative, radial, normalized, and C² with compact support; Wε(z)=ε^(−d)W(z/ε). Integrals are compactly supported Riemann integrals, taken componentwise for vector integrands. Vector norms are Euclidean and multilinear derivative norms are induced operator norms.
The gradient operator differentiates the evaluation variable: Dεf(x)=∫f(y)∇Wε(x−y)dy.

SPH has fixed positive masses, fixed ε>0, P∈C¹((0,∞)×R,R), densities including self terms, and domain U where every density is positive. Its internal-energy equation is exactly ė_i=A_iΣ_jm_j(v_i−v_j)·∇Wε(q_i−q_j).
The quantitative Lipschitz estimate requires a nonempty compact convex subset of U and uses the maximum of Euclidean position/velocity block norms and absolute internal-energy coordinates.
Euler uses exact initial data and h=T/n. The exact solution must exist throughout [0,T] with distance at least δ>0 from Kᶜ; the sufficient step condition is E_h<δ. When L=0, E_h=0.

load_bearing.statement: For every ε>0, supp Wε⊂closed B(0,Rε), ∫Wε=1, ∫zWε(z)dz=0, and ∫|z|²Wε(z)dz=ε²m₂. Pointwise, ∇Wε(z)=ε^(−d−1)∇W(z/ε) and D²Wε(z)=ε^(−d−2)D²W(z/ε); consequently their sup norms equal ε^(−d−1)M₁ and ε^(−d−2)M₂.
For the defined SPH system, g_ij=∇Wε(q_i−q_j) and F_ij=−m_im_j(A_i+A_j)g_ij satisfy g_ji=−g_ij and g_ii=0; for i≠j, F_ji=−F_ij, and F_ij is parallel to q_i−q_j, allowing the zero vector.
For compactly supported Lipschitz g with supp(g)⊂Ω and the defined cell rule, |∫Ωg−Q_hg|≤Σ_{j∈J_g}V_j osc_{C_j}(g)≤2hL_gΣ_{j∈J_g}V_j, where J_g consists of cells meeting supp(g).
For the admissible W and coordinate indices j,k,l, ∫∂_kW=0, ∫z_j∂_kW=−δ_jk, and ∫z_jz_l∂_kW=0. Also m₃=∫|z|³|∇W(z)|dz is finite.

On a nonempty compact convex K⊂U, with ||z||#=max_i{|q_i|,|v_i|,|e_i|}, M=Σ_im_i, V=sup_K max_i|v_i|, K₁=||∇Wε||∞, K₂=||D²Wε||∞, a=P/ρ², A₀=max_{K,i}|a(ρ_i,e_i)|, Aρ=max_{K,i}|∂ρa(ρ_i,e_i)|, Ae=max_{K,i}|∂ea(ρ_i,e_i)|, and A_Lip=2MK₁Aρ+Ae, F is Lipschitz with constant max{1,M(2K₁A_Lip+4A₀K₂),2MVA_LipK₁+2MA₀K₁+4MA₀VK₂}.

For the defined cell rule, h≤ε≤1, an interior x, and bounded f∈C¹(R^d) with bounded first derivative, a constant C=C(d,R,C_L,W) independent of ε,h,x gives |Q⁰−Sεf|≤Ch(||∇f||∞+ε^(−1)||f||∞) and |Q¹−Dεf|≤Ch(ε^(−1)||∇f||∞+ε^(−2)||f||∞).
For the defined SPH system, U={z:ρ_i(q)>0 for every i} is open and F is continuous and locally Lipschitz on U. From each initial state z₀∈U there is a unique local C¹ solution.
